clue.text: Mother takes in dogs

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother
to take someone in is to cheat them, and to stiff someone is slang for cheating them out of money

explanation.surface: A mother gives a home to some stray dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' looks like an act of kindness, but here it means 'cheats', which is STIFFS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastiffs are a breed of large, powerful guard dog.

clue.text: Warnings from nearly all branches

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: arms are branches, as of a tree or a river

explanation.surface: Warnings come from almost every branch of an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarms are signals that alert people to danger.

clue.text: Restricted a part of car with raised temperature

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a letter lifts it higher up the column, to the top

parts.note: the boot is the British word for a car's trunk

explanation.surface: Part of a car is out of bounds because it is overheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' takes the final T of ABOOT up to the front of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom, so it is restricted.

clue.text: Helped hide followers of explorer Erik

parts.note: fur is an animal's hide or pelt
the Viking explorer is Erik the Red, so the words after Erik are THE RED

explanation.surface: Someone helped hide the descendants of a Viking explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb, but it is a noun, FUR. Erik the Red was the Norse explorer who founded the first settlement in Greenland.
explanation.definitionFit: To further a cause is to advance or promote it, which is to help it.

clue.text: Least clever son most humble

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees
lowest means humblest, lowest in rank

explanation.surface: A modest son is said to be the dimmest in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow means dim-witted, so the slowest person is the least bright.

clue.text: Worship silver in cups

indicators.note: to cup something is to hold it in curved hands, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: someone who is in is at home, so HOME stands for in
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver trophies are prized almost like sacred objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silver in cups' looks like a trophy cabinet, but 'in' is a piece in its own right (at home), and 'cups' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is reverent respect or honour shown to someone, close to worship.

clue.text: Deity from hot area acts without love

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: does means acts or performs
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A god emerges from a hot place and acts without love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot area' hints at the underworld itself, but it only gives H and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek god of the underworld, as well as the name of his realm.

clue.text: Put explosives on handle and access passage

parts.note: mines are buried explosive devices
a haft is the handle of a knife, axe or tool

explanation.surface: Someone lays explosives and deals with an access tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Put ... on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineshaft is the vertical passage giving access to the workings of a mine.

clue.text: Pungent scrap turned over tongue unknown

indicators.note: in a down clue turning over flips the word, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
to tongue something is to lick it
Y is a mathematical unknown, like X and Z

explanation.surface: A cheese-like scrap of food is turned over on an unfamiliar tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' looks like a noun, but it is a verb, LICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic has a strong, sharp smell and taste, so something garlicky is pungent.

clue.text: Curvature hard to miss in cavern

indicators.note: missing something means going without it, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a chamber is a large cave or hollow space, like a cavern
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A potholer finds the curve of a cave roof hard to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Camber is the slight convex curve built into a road surface or a ship's deck.

clue.text: Link to alternative journal about new normal

parts.note: OR is the word that introduces an alternative

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the journal word goes round the letter

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

explanation.surface: Someone wants to link to another journal's piece on the 'new normal'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Link to' only joins the definition to the wordplay. 'new normal' looks like a stock phrase, but 'new' belongs to the wordplay and 'normal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary and normal are synonyms, both meaning usual or unremarkable.

clue.text: One seemingly delightful drink

definitions.meaning: a suave, charming person whose charm may not be sincere

explanation.surface: Someone describes a drink that only looks delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a charming smooth-talker and a thick blended fruit drink.

clue.text: Flier is about film

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is is read backwards

parts.note: a skin is a thin film or covering layer

explanation.surface: A pilot or aviator is the subject of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests an aviator, but it means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Evidence of delivery time given by shop informally

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a term of time in prison
Marks is the informal name for Marks & Spencer, a British high-street department store

explanation.surface: A courier's shop needs proof of delivery times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests parcels, but it means childbirth. MARKS (Marks & Spencer) is a British chain store selling clothes and food.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretch marks are scars on the skin that pregnancy and childbirth often leave behind.

clue.text: Lifeline thrown Aston Villa after losing lead to Liverpool

indicators.note: thrown means upset or disordered, so the team name's letters are rearranged
losing shows that a letter must be taken from the pool before rearranging
the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Aston Villa are thrown a lifeline after losing a lead to Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa and Liverpool are English football clubs. Take one L out of ASTON VILLA and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvation is rescue from danger or ruin, as a lifeline gives.

clue.text: Mineral regularly cheaper — it is in China

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken
is in means the word goes inside the other

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate)

explanation.surface: A mineral that is reliably cheaper is to be found in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Haematite is a reddish-black mineral that is the main ore of iron.

clue.text: Could that be article in upended box for guest?

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
in a down clue upending turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: the box is informal for television, TV
the question 'is it?' asks whether that could be the case
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if an item in an upturned box belongs to a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is the telly, TV, which 'upended' turns to VT.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitant is a visitor, especially a supernatural one, so a guest.

clue.text: Speak against Masons? Time for expulsion

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for speaking against or disrespecting them
Freemasons meet in lodges, so they are lodge men

explanation.surface: Criticising the Freemasons gets someone thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dislodgement is the act of forcing something or someone out of position, an ousting.

clue.text: Explosive set off covering rock's opening cracks

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round something, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
explosive means blown apart, so the letters are rearranged
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An explosive is detonated to crack open rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' rearranges SET OFF to EFFOTS, which goes round R. 'cracks' looks like a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a crack at something is to have a go, so cracks are attempts or efforts.

clue.text: Duck's rest, dropping wings and head

indicators.note: wings are the outer edges, so losing them leaves the middle letters

parts.note: a cape is a headland, a head jutting out to sea

explanation.surface: A duck rests and loses its wings and head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a bird, but it is the verb meaning dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or evade it, which is escaping it.

clue.text: Coarse lubricated drunk, not awfully cute

indicators.note: drunk means scrambled, so the letters of lubricated are rearranged
not shows letters are taken away, and awfully says those letters can come out in any order

explanation.surface: A drunk, oiled with drink, is not exactly adorable.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of LUBRICATED, minus C, U, T, E, can be rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald humour is vulgar and bawdy, which is coarse.

clue.text: Eccentric exuberant replacing stuffing in dolly

indicators.note: the stuffing is the inside of a word, and replacing it swaps those inner letters for the new piece

parts.note: OTT means over the top, excessive or exuberant

explanation.surface: An eccentric, exuberant person restuffs a doll.
explanation.walkthrough: The stuffing of DOLLY is OLL; OTT takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty is informal for slightly mad or batty, so it means eccentric.

clue.text: Daring thief earl essentially apprehends

indicators.note: to apprehend is to catch or hold, so these words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A bold burglar is in effect arrested by an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across thiEF EARL ESSentially; even 'essentially' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fearless person has no fear, and so is daring.

clue.text: Grand spread, left for male

indicators.note: putting one letter for another means it replaces it

parts.note: marge is short for margarine, a spread for bread

explanation.surface: A grand feast is spread out, left for the men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' suggests a feast, but it is margarine (MARGE).
explanation.definitionFit: Large and grand both describe something big or imposing in scale.

clue.text: Returned wine, second-rate one found on flight

parts.note: B is a mark for second class, so it stands for second-rate

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the wine is read backwards

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

explanation.surface: A passenger sends back a mediocre wine on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail running up a staircase, and a staircase is called a flight.

clue.text: Offensive northern radio broadcast hosts

indicators.note: to host is to hold a guest inside, so the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Radio presenters in the north air something offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns RADIO into IROAD, which 'hosts' N.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is an advance or raid into enemy territory, which an offensive is.

clue.text: Not giving smart reply in the end

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so this picks the last letter

explanation.surface: Someone ends up with no clever comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingy person is mean and reluctant to give or share anything.

clue.text: Trimmed distorted beetroot, fixed for cooking

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, so the last letter is taken off

parts.note: skewed means distorted or slanted
beetroot is famously red, as in going beetroot with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A cook trims misshapen beetroot and fixes it for the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is skewered has been pierced and fixed on a skewer ready for grilling.
